GridLayoutComponent and GridItemComponent — the two standalone components this package exports.

The package exports these from its main entry point — both are
**standalone components**, added directly to your own component's
`imports` array, no `NgModule` required:

| Component | Selector | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| [`GridLayoutComponent`](/angular/components/grid-layout/props/) | `kdl-grid-layout` | The grid container — owns the layout array, breakpoints, and collision/compaction logic. A fully controlled component (`layout` `@Input()` + `layoutChange` `@Output()`). |
| [`GridItemComponent`](/angular/components/grid-item/props/) | `kdl-grid-item` | A single draggable/resizable cell, projected as content of `GridLayoutComponent`. |

See [Styling](/angular/components/styling/) once that page lands for
the CSS custom properties and class names used throughout.

```ts
import { GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/angular';
```

There's no default export — always import by name. See
[Installation](/angular/guide/installation/) if you haven't added the
package yet.

This package also has real, exported close-button and drag-handle
components, matching Vue and React — but note that `GridItemComponent`'s
own built-in close button (`showCloseButton` + a `removeItem`
`@Output()` you handle yourself) is a separate, simpler path most
consumers should reach for first; the standalone components below are
for a consumer who wants the same building blocks rendered somewhere
else entirely (e.g. inside a custom header). Any part of a
`GridItemComponent` is already a drag handle by default — restrict it
via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom` directly on `GridItemComponent`,
without needing the standalone drag-handle component below at all,
unless you want its specific rendered widget.

## Standalone utility components

Two additional standalone components exist for a consumer who wants
the same close-button/drag-handle *building blocks* Vue's own
`CustomCloseButton.vue`/`CustomDragElement.vue` provide, used outside
`GridItemComponent`'s own built-in rendering entirely — e.g. placed
inside a custom header region (see `GridItemHeaderDirective` above).
Neither is used internally by `GridLayoutComponent`/`GridItemComponent`
themselves; a consumer opts into either explicitly.

| Component | Selector | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GridItemCloseButtonComponent` | `kdl-custom-close-button` | A standalone close button. Takes a required `i` — the id of whichever item it should remove — and emits `removeGridItem` with that id on click; wire that output to your own removal logic. |


## A real, notable difference from React

Unlike the React package (where `GridItem` only takes `i`, reading
everything else — position, size, `isDraggable`, and so on — off the
matching entry in `GridLayout`'s own `layout` array), `GridItemComponent`
here takes `i`/`x`/`y`/`w`/`h` as its **own, direct, required
`@Input()`s** — the same shape Vue's `GridItem` uses. You bind each one
explicitly per item in your own template's `@for` loop; this component
doesn't read them off `layout` automatically.

## The imperative API

`GridLayoutComponent` also exposes public methods, reached via a
template reference variable (`#grid` + `@ViewChild` in your own
component, or a plain template variable for a direct template call) —
`compactNow()`/`rearrange()`, `duplicateItem(id)`, `undo()`/`redo()`
(plus the `canUndo`/`canRedo` public fields), `selectItem()`/
`deselectItem()`/`toggleItemSelection()`/`clearSelection()`,
`alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`, `exportLayoutAsSvg()`,
and `scrollToItem(id)`/`focusItem(id)` — the Angular equivalent of
Vue's own `defineExpose`'d template-ref methods, or React's `ref`-based
imperative handle. See [Public members](/angular/api/) once that page
lands for the full reference.

## Drag & resize

- **Drag anywhere, or from a handle.** Every item is draggable by default; restrict it to a specific handle with `dragAllowFrom`, or exclude specific elements with `dragIgnoreFrom` (and `resizeIgnoreFrom` for resize specifically).
- **Resize from any edge or corner** — top, right, bottom, left, and the diagonals — with optional `preserveAspectRatio` locking.
- **Min/max size constraints** (`minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`) per item.
- **Bounded dragging** (`isBounded`) — keep items from being dragged outside the container.
- **Static items** — lock specific items in place; they ignore dragging/resizing entirely and act as fixed obstacles for compaction.
- **Per-item `zIndex` override** — pin one item permanently above every other, including while others are mid-resize, regardless of the library's own implicit static/resizing stacking rules.
- **A separate header region** — a `GridItemHeaderDirective` marker directive (`[kdlGridItemHeader]`) applied to your own header content, projected into `GridItemComponent`'s own dedicated header region instead of its plain default content. Angular's equivalent of Vue's named slot or React's `header` render prop, expressed as a queryable content-projection marker instead.
- **Per-item `autoHeight`** — a live-resyncing height, driven by a real `ResizeObserver` on the item's own content rather than a one-time measurement.
- **`dragActivationDistance`** — a per-pointer-type drag-start threshold, so a small accidental movement doesn't immediately start a drag.

## Layout & collision

- **Automatic compaction.** Items fill gaps vertically by default; other items automatically move out of the way of a drag/resize.
- **Pluggable compaction strategy** (`compactType`) — five built-in strategies (vertical, horizontal, none, and overlap variants of each), or replace the algorithm entirely with a custom `compactor` `@Input()`.
- **Horizontal shift mode** (`horizontalShift`) — push colliding items left/right instead of down.
- **Prevent collision mode** (`preventCollision`) — block a drag/resize instead of pushing other items, with a `moveBlockedByCollision` `@Output()` so a consumer can give feedback the moment that happens.
- **Magnetic snap-to-grid** (`snapToGrid`/`snapThreshold`) — actually adjusts an item's landing position to align with a neighbor, not just a visual guide.
- **Alignment guides** (`showAlignmentGuides`) — Figma-style guide lines while dragging or resizing, wherever an item's edges line up with another's.
- **`restoreOnDrag`** — keep other items from compacting past their pre-drag position while a drag is in progress.
- **Auto-sizing container** — the grid's height grows/shrinks to fit its content by default (`autoSize`, or the newer `heightMode` `@Input()` for finer control including `'scroll'`/`'fit'` modes).
- **Spacing indicators** (`showSpacingGuides`) — a labeled distance badge (e.g. "2 cols") in the gap between the active item and its nearest neighbor on each side, independently toggleable alongside alignment guides.
- **Serializable layout.** The `layout` array is a plain, JSON-serializable structure you own — persist it anywhere.
- **Named layout presets** (`GridLayoutPresetsService`) — save and switch between multiple named arrangements, layered on the same serialize/restore primitives `GridLayoutStorageService` uses.
- **Grid-to-SVG export** (`exportLayoutAsSvg()`, a public method on `GridLayoutComponent`) — a dependency-free utility producing a standalone SVG snapshot of the current layout.
- **Undo/redo** (`enableUndoRedo`, capped via `undoHistoryLimit`) — opt-in history at committed-change granularity (drag/resize end, add/remove), not per intermediate frame. Reach `undo()`/`redo()` and the `canUndo`/`canRedo` flags via a template reference variable on `GridLayoutComponent`.
- **Add/remove items freely**, with automatic re-compaction — no manual position math required. `duplicateItem(id)` (also a public method) clones an existing item into a collision-safe spot below it.
- **`distributeEvenly`** — spreads an out-of-bounds item to the next available slot on a responsive breakpoint change, instead of clamping it to the right edge.

## Multi-select & group operations

- **Select multiple items** (`multiSelect`) — click to select, Ctrl/Cmd+click to add additively, click empty background to clear, and **Shift-click to select a contiguous range** from the last-clicked anchor.
- **Group move and resize** — drag or resize any selected item and the rest of the selection moves or resizes by the same delta, from mouse or keyboard alike.
- **Align/distribute commands** (`alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`, public methods on `GridLayoutComponent`) — align a selection to an edge, or evenly space what's between.

## Responsive

- **Breakpoint-based column counts**, with sensible defaults and fully customizable `breakpoints`/`cols`.
- **Pre-defined layouts per breakpoint** (`responsiveLayouts`), for full control over how content reflows instead of relying on auto-generation.

## Internationalization

- **RTL mirroring** (`isMirrored`) for an entire layout or individual items — positions (and dragging) flip horizontally with a single `@Input()`. The resize-specific edge-swap math for RTL is a direct analogy to the LTR case rather than exhaustively verified against a real browser — the same "best-effort" caveat this package's own source carries for that one corner.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard move & resize.** Every non-static, editable item is keyboard-focusable — arrow keys move it, Shift+arrow keys resize it — without needing any extra configuration, including RTL-aware key direction and `multiSelect` group-move/resize engagement.
- **Screen reader support** — interactive items are announced with an item-role description and a description of the available keyboard controls; visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
- **Localizable ARIA strings** (`ariaLabels`) — the close button's label, role description, and the keyboard move/resize instructions are overridable (`GridLayoutComponent` grid-wide default, `GridItemComponent` per-item override), rather than hardcoded English literals.

## Cross-grid & external drag-and-drop

- **Drag items from outside the grid** (`allowOutsideDrop`) using the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop API, with a live drop-position placeholder while dragging over the grid.
- **Drag items between two independent grids** (`allowCrossGridDrag`/`disableExternalDrop`/`layoutId`) via a real first-fit bin-pack, not a naive placement then compaction sorts out.
- **Multiple grids on one page** with zero shared state — each `GridLayoutComponent` provides its own, independent `GridEventBusService` instance — beyond an optional `layoutId`.

## Styling & customization

- **Unstyled-by-default content** — `GridItemComponent`'s projected content holds whatever you put there; the library only handles position/size.
- **Built-in close button** (`showCloseButton` + a `removeItem` `@Output()` you handle yourself), and any part of an item is a drag handle by default, restrictable via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom`. Standalone `GridItemCloseButtonComponent`/`GridItemDragHandleComponent` also exist for the same building blocks used outside `GridItemComponent`'s own rendering entirely (e.g. inside a custom header) — see [Components](/angular/components/) for both.
- **Configurable border radius** per item (`borderRadiusPx`/`useBorderRadius`, grid-wide default + per-item override).
- **Optional grid line guides** (`showGridLines`), useful while building a layout or as a permanent visual aid.
- **Configurable transition duration/easing** (`transitionDurationMs`/`transitionTimingFunction`), applied via CSS custom properties.
- **Configurable resize-hint appearance** (`showResizeHandles`/`resizeHandleColor`, grid-wide default + per-item override), plus a per-item `resizeHandles` `@Input()` restricting which of the 8 edges/corners actually activate.

## Developer experience

- **Full TypeScript support.** Every component, directive, service, and interface is typed and exported from the package's main entry point — see [API](/angular/api/) once that page lands.
- **Zero runtime dependencies beyond Angular and RxJS.** The drag/resize engine is built on native Pointer Events, not a third-party library — the same shared engine the Vue and React packages use.
- **The same framework-agnostic core** (`@keystone-dashboard-layout/core`) Vue and React use for their own grid-layout math (collision detection, movement, compaction, and more) — all three packages share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong parts.
- **Idiomatic Angular.** Standalone components (no `NgModule` required), a DI-scoped `GridEventBusService` instead of Vue's `provide`/`inject` or React's Context, `providedIn: 'root'` services instead of ref-bound composables/hooks, and a marker directive queried via `@ContentChild` instead of a named slot or render prop — the same underlying behavior, expressed the way Angular actually works.
- **Tested, with one real gap.** A genuine unit/component test suite (Jest + `jest-preset-angular`) backs every phase, and Stryker mutation testing is configured — see the package's own `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the phase-by-phase history. Unlike Vue and React, this package doesn't yet have a real end-to-end browser test layer (Karma is present but reserved for a possible future one, not currently used for anything) — a genuine, open gap rather than an oversight this page should paper over.

## Drag & resize

- **Drag anywhere, or from a handle.** Every item is draggable by default; restrict it to a specific handle with `dragAllowFrom`, or exclude specific elements with `dragIgnoreFrom` (and `resizeIgnoreFrom` for resize specifically).
- **Resize from any edge or corner** — top, right, bottom, left, and the diagonals — with optional `preserveAspectRatio` locking.
- **Min/max size constraints** (`minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`) per item.
- **Bounded dragging** (`isBounded`) — keep items from being dragged outside the container.
- **Static items** — lock specific items in place; they ignore dragging/resizing entirely and act as fixed obstacles for compaction.
- **Per-item `zIndex` override** — pin one item permanently above every other, including while others are mid-resize, regardless of the library's own implicit static/resizing stacking rules.
- **A separate header region** (the `header` render prop on `GridItem`) — an optional header area above an item's own main content, its own scrollable region taking whatever space remains.
- **Per-item `autoHeight`** — a live-resyncing height, driven by a real `ResizeObserver` on the item's own content rather than a one-time measurement.
- **`dragActivationDistance`** — a per-pointer-type drag-start threshold, so a small accidental movement doesn't immediately start a drag.

## Layout & collision

- **Automatic compaction.** Items fill gaps vertically by default; other items automatically move out of the way of a drag/resize.
- **Pluggable compaction strategy** (`compactType`) — five built-in strategies (vertical, horizontal, none, and overlap variants of each), or replace the algorithm entirely with a custom `compactor` prop.
- **Horizontal shift mode** — push colliding items left/right instead of down.
- **Prevent collision mode** (`preventCollision`) — block a drag/resize instead of pushing other items, with an `onMoveBlockedByCollision(id)` callback so a consumer can give feedback the moment that happens.
- **Magnetic snap-to-grid** (`snapToGrid`/`snapThreshold`) — actually adjusts an item's landing position to align with a neighbor, not just a visual guide.
- **Alignment guides** (`showAlignmentGuides`) — Figma-style guide lines while dragging or resizing, wherever an item's edges line up with another's.
- **`restoreOnDrag`** — keep other items from compacting past their pre-drag position while a drag is in progress.
- **Auto-sizing container** — the grid's height grows/shrinks to fit its content by default (`autoSize`, or the newer `heightMode` prop for finer control including `'scroll'`/`'fit'` modes).
- **Spacing indicators** (`showSpacingGuides`) — a labeled distance badge (e.g. "2 cols") in the gap between the active item and its nearest neighbor on each side, independently toggleable alongside alignment guides.
- **Serializable layout.** The `layout` array is a plain, JSON-serializable structure you own — persist it anywhere.
- **Named layout presets** (`useLayoutPresets`) — save and switch between multiple named arrangements, layered on the same serialize/restore primitives.
- **Grid-to-SVG export** (`exportLayoutAsSvg()` on the imperative handle) — a dependency-free utility producing a standalone SVG snapshot of the current layout.
- **Undo/redo** (`enableUndoRedo`, capped via `undoHistoryLimit`) — opt-in history at committed-change granularity (drag/resize end, add/remove), not per intermediate frame.
- **Add/remove items freely**, with automatic re-compaction — no manual position math required.
- **`distributeEvenly`** — spreads an out-of-bounds item to the next available slot on a responsive breakpoint change, instead of clamping it to the right edge.

## Multi-select & group operations

- **Select multiple items** (`multiSelect`) — click to select, Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+click to add additively, click empty background to clear.
- **Group move and resize** — drag or resize any selected item and the rest of the selection moves or resizes by the same delta, from mouse or keyboard alike.
- **Align/distribute commands** (`alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)` on the imperative handle) — align a selection to an edge, or evenly space what's between.

## Responsive

- **Breakpoint-based column counts**, with sensible defaults and fully customizable `breakpoints`/`cols`.
- **Pre-defined layouts per breakpoint** (`responsiveLayouts`), for full control over how content reflows instead of relying on auto-generation.

## Internationalization

- **RTL mirroring** (`isMirrored`) for an entire layout or individual items (per-item opt-out via `ILayoutItem.isMirrored`) — positions (and dragging) flip horizontally with a single prop.

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard move & resize.** Every non-static, editable item is keyboard-focusable — arrow keys move it, Shift+arrow keys resize it — without needing any extra configuration, including RTL-aware key direction and `multiSelect` group-move/resize engagement.
- **Screen reader support** — interactive items are announced with an item-role description and a description of the available keyboard controls; visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
- **Localizable ARIA strings** (`ariaLabels`) — the close button's label, role description, and the keyboard move/resize instructions are overridable (`GridLayout` grid-wide default, `GridItem` per-item override), rather than hardcoded English literals.

## Cross-grid & external drag-and-drop

- **Drag items from outside the grid** (`allowOutsideDrop`) using the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop API, with a live drop-position placeholder while dragging over the grid.
- **Drag items between two independent grids** (`allowCrossGridDrag`/`disableExternalDrop`/`layoutId`) via a real first-fit bin-pack, not a naive placement then compaction sorts out.
- **Multiple grids on one page** with zero shared state or configuration beyond an optional `layoutId`.

## Styling & customization

- **Unstyled-by-default content** — `GridItem`'s children hold whatever you put there; the library only handles position/size.
- **Built-in close button** (`showCloseButton` + an `onItemClose` callback you handle yourself), and any part of an item is a drag handle by default, restrictable via `dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom` — there's no separate exported close-button or drag-handle component to import.
- **Configurable border radius** per item (`borderRadiusPx`/`useBorderRadius`, grid-wide default + per-item override).
- **Optional grid line guides** (`showGridLines`), useful while building a layout or as a permanent visual aid.
- **Configurable transition duration/easing** (`transitionDurationMs`/`transitionTimingFunction`), applied via CSS custom properties.

## Developer experience

- **Full TypeScript support.** Every prop, callback, and interface is typed and exported from the package's main entry point — see [API](/react/api/) once that page lands.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** The drag/resize engine is built on native Pointer Events, not a third-party library — the same shared engine the Vue package uses.
- **The same framework-agnostic core** (`@keystone-dashboard-layout/core`) Vue uses for its own grid-layout math (collision detection, movement, compaction, and more) — both packages share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong parts.
- **Idiomatic React.** A fully controlled component (`layout`/`onLayoutChange`), hooks instead of composables, Context instead of `provide`/`inject`, render props instead of named slots, and a `ref`-based imperative handle instead of `defineExpose` — the same underlying behavior, expressed the way React actually works.
- **Well-tested.** A real unit, mutation, and end-to-end test suite backs the package — see the package's own `docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the phase-by-phase history.

- **Spacing indicators** — a labeled distance badge (e.g. "2 cols") in the gap between the active item and its nearest neighbor on each side (`showSpacingGuides`), independently toggleable alongside alignment guides.
- **Serializable layout.** The `layout` array is a plain, JSON-serializable structure you own — persist it anywhere. See [v-model & save/load layout](/vue/examples/save-load-layout/).
- **Named layout presets** (`useLayoutPresets`) — save and switch between multiple named arrangements, layered on the same serialize/restore primitives. See [Named layout presets](/vue/examples/named-presets/).
- **Grid-to-SVG export** (`exportLayoutAsSvg`) — a dependency-free utility producing a standalone SVG snapshot of the current layout. See [Export layout as SVG](/vue/examples/svg-export/).
- **Undo/redo** (`enableUndoRedo`, capped via `undoHistoryLimit`) — opt-in history at committed-change granularity (drag/resize end, add/remove), not per intermediate frame. See [Undo/redo](/vue/examples/undo-redo/).
- **Add/remove items freely**, with automatic re-compaction — no manual position math required. See [Add or remove items](/vue/examples/add-remove-items/).

## Multi-select & group operations

- **Select multiple items** — click to select, Shift/Ctrl/Cmd+click to add additively, click empty background to clear.
- **Group move and resize** — drag or resize any selected item and the rest of the selection moves or resizes by the same delta, from mouse or keyboard alike. See [Multi-select & group move/resize](/vue/examples/multi-select-group-move-resize/).

## Responsive

- **Breakpoint-based column counts**, with sensible defaults (`xxl`/`xl`/`lg`/`md`/`sm`/`xs`/`xxs`) and fully customizable breakpoints/columns. See [Responsive breakpoints](/vue/examples/responsive-breakpoints/).
- **Pre-defined layouts per breakpoint**, for full control over how content reflows instead of relying on auto-generation. See [Responsive predefined layouts](/vue/examples/responsive-predefined-layouts/).

## Internationalization

- **RTL mirroring** for an entire layout or individual items — positions (and dragging) flip horizontally with a single prop. See [Mirrored (RTL)](/vue/examples/mirrored-rtl/).

## Accessibility

- **Keyboard move & resize.** Every non-static, editable item is keyboard-focusable — arrow keys move it, Shift+arrow keys resize it — without needing any extra configuration. Reuses the exact same events/collision handling the mouse-driven path uses. See [Accessibility scope](/vue/guide/project/accessibility/) for the full scope, including what's deliberately not (yet) covered.
- **Screen reader support** — interactive items are announced with `role="group"` and a description of the available keyboard controls; visible focus indicator for keyboard users.
- **Localizable ARIA strings** (`ariaLabels`) — the close button's label, `aria-roledescription`, and the keyboard move/resize instructions are overridable (`GridLayout` grid-wide default, `GridItem` per-item override), rather than hardcoded English literals. See [Localizable ARIA strings](/vue/examples/aria-labels/).

## Cross-grid & external drag-and-drop

- **Drag items from outside the grid** using the browser's native HTML5 drag-and-drop API. See [Drag, drop from outside](/vue/examples/outside-drag-drop/).
- **Drag items between two independent grids.** See [Drag, drop from grid to grid](/vue/examples/cross-grid-drag-drop/).
- **Multiple grids on one page** with zero shared state or configuration. See [Multiple grids](/vue/examples/multiple-grids/).

## Styling & customization

- **Unstyled-by-default content** — `GridItem`'s slot holds whatever you put there; the library only handles position/size.
- **Built-in close button**, or bring your own via the exported `CustomCloseButton`/`CustomDragElement` components. See [Show close button](/vue/examples/close-button/) and [Custom drag handle & close button](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/).
- **Configurable border radius** per item. See [Border radius](/vue/examples/border-radius/).
- **Optional grid line guides**, useful while building a layout or as a permanent visual aid. See [Show grid lines](/vue/examples/grid-lines/).
- **CSS custom properties and SCSS variables** for deeper theming — see [Styling → Variables](/vue/components/styling/css-variables/).

## Developer experience

- **Full TypeScript support.** Every prop, event, enum, and interface is typed and exported from the package's main entry point — see [API](/vue/api/).
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** The drag/resize engine is built on native Pointer Events, not a third-party library — no `interact.js` or equivalent to audit or update.
- **A separate, framework-agnostic core entry point** exposing this library's own grid-layout math (collision detection, movement, compaction, and more) with zero Vue dependency and no live-DOM requirement — usable standalone, e.g. for server-side layout validation.
- **Vue 3 Composition API**, built with `<script setup>` throughout — works equally well with the Options API in consuming projects.
- **Well-tested.** A full unit, component, and end-to-end test suite backs every release — see [Production readiness](/vue/guide/project/production-readiness/) for the current numbers.

What Keystone Dashboard Layout for Angular is, what you get, and where to go next.

Keystone Dashboard Layout for Angular is an Angular component library for
building draggable, resizable, responsive dashboard grids — the kind of
UI you'd use for a customizable analytics dashboard, a widget board, or
any screen where users rearrange content themselves.

It's a TypeScript-first library built on the exact same shared
`@keystone-dashboard-layout/core` algorithms and native, Pointer
Events-based drag/resize engine the Vue and React packages use — all
three frameworks share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-
subtly-wrong parts (collision, compaction, responsive breakpoint math)
rather than each maintaining their own copy. Angular has reached full
feature parity with both.

## What you get

- **`GridLayoutComponent`** (selector `kdl-grid-layout`) — the
  container. A **fully controlled** component: it never mutates the
  `layout` array (or any item in it) you pass in — every drag/resize
  tick (and the compaction that follows it) is reported via a
  `layoutChange` `@Output()` with a brand-new array. The same
  controlled-data-flow contract the React package uses, rather than
  Vue's own two-way `v-model:layout` binding.
- **`GridItemComponent`** (selector `kdl-grid-item`) — a single
  draggable/resizable cell. Unlike the React package, position and
  size are this component's **own direct `@Input()`s** (`i`/`x`/`y`/
  `w`/`h`, all required) rather than fields read off a matching layout
  item — you bind each one explicitly in your own template's `@for`
  loop, the same shape Vue's own `GridItem` uses.
- **Public imperative methods on `GridLayoutComponent`** — reached via
  a template reference variable (`#grid` + `@ViewChild`), the Angular
  equivalent of Vue's `defineExpose`'d template-ref methods or React's
  `ref`-based imperative handle: `compactNow()`, `rearrange()`,
  `duplicateItem(id)`, `undo()`/`redo()`, `selectItem()`/
  `clearSelection()`, `alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`,
  `exportLayoutAsSvg()`, `scrollToItem(id)`/`focusItem(id)`, and more.
- **`GridLayoutStorageService`** and **`GridLayoutPresetsService`**
  (both `providedIn: 'root'`) — injectable services wrapping layout
  persistence (serializing to/from `localStorage`) and named layout
  presets. Unlike Vue's ref-bound composables, every method here
  takes/returns a plain layout value directly — you call `save()`/
  `load()` from wherever you already own your own `layout` state.
- **`GridItemHeaderDirective`** — a marker directive
  (`[kdlGridItemHeader]`) applied to your own header content, letting
  `GridItemComponent` project it into a dedicated header region instead
  of its plain default content.

There's also a real, exported close-button component
(`GridItemCloseButtonComponent`) and drag-handle component
(`GridItemDragHandleComponent`), matching Vue and React — useful when
you want those same building blocks rendered somewhere other than
`GridItemComponent`'s own built-in rendering (e.g. inside a custom
header). Most consumers should reach for the simpler, built-in path
first though: a close button is a built-in, per-item opt-in
(`showCloseButton` + a `removeItem` `@Output()` you handle yourself),
and any part of an item is a drag handle by default, restrictable via
`dragAllowFrom`/`dragIgnoreFrom`.

## How it fits together

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/angular';
import type { TLayout } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/core';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-dashboard',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent],
  template: `
    <kdl-grid-layout [layout]="layout" (layoutChange)="layout = $event">
      @for (item of layout; track item.i) {
        <kdl-grid-item [i]="item.i" [x]="item.x" [y]="item.y" [w]="item.w" [h]="item.h">
          Item {{ item.i }}
        </kdl-grid-item>
      }
    </kdl-grid-layout>
  `,
})
export class DashboardComponent {
  layout: TLayout = [
    { i: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
    { i: 'b', x: 2, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
  ];
}
```

`layout` is a plain array of `{ i, x, y, w, h, ... }` objects. You own
that array; `layoutChange` hands you a new one every time the user
drags or resizes something, and you decide what to do with it (usually
just reassigning your own field, as above). `GridItemComponent` itself
still needs `x`/`y`/`w`/`h` bound explicitly per item — this component
doesn't read them off `layout` automatically the way React's `GridItem`
does. Everything else (collision resolution, compaction, responsive
breakpoint switching) happens automatically based on the props you set
on `GridLayoutComponent`.

## Design goals

A few decisions that shape how the library behaves, worth knowing up
front:

- **You own the data.** `layout` is a plain, serializable array you
  control — the library never mutates it in place, only ever hands you
  a new one via `layoutChange`.
- **Sensible defaults, explicit overrides.** Most behavior (draggable,
  resizable, bounded, etc.) can be set once on `GridLayoutComponent`
  and inherited by every item via a DI-scoped event bus, or overridden
  per-item when needed.
- **Idiomatic Angular, not a literal Vue-to-Angular transliteration.**
  Vue's `provide`/`inject` eventBus becomes an injectable,
  component-scoped `GridEventBusService`; its composables become
  `providedIn: 'root'` services; its named slots become a marker
  directive (`GridItemHeaderDirective`) queried via `@ContentChild`;
  and its reactive two-way binding becomes the standard `@Input()`/
  `@Output()` pattern — the same underlying behavior, expressed the
  way Angular actually works.

Unlike the Vue package (which bakes most of its own defaults into
compile-time SCSS variables, mostly not runtime-overridable), this
package's stylesheet uses real, runtime-overridable CSS custom
properties throughout, under a consistent `kdl-` prefix on every class
name — confirmed directly from `packages/react/src/styles/index.css`.

## CSS custom properties

All of these are genuinely overridable from your own stylesheet after
importing `@keystone-dashboard-layout/react/style.css`:

| Property | Default | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| `--kdl-transition-duration` | `200ms` | `transitionDurationMs` prop |
| `--kdl-transition-timing` | `ease` | `transitionTimingFunction` prop |
| `--kdl-grid-line-column-size` | `1px` | Computed from `colNum`/margin when `showGridLines` is on |
| `--kdl-grid-line-row-size` | `1px` | Computed from `rowHeight`/margin when `showGridLines` is on |
| `--kdl-resize-handle-color` | `rgb(94 94 94 / 45%)` | `resizeHandleColor` prop |

```css
/* After importing '@keystone-dashboard-layout/react/style.css' */
.kdl-grid-layout {
  --kdl-resize-handle-color: #38bdf8;
}
```

## Key class names

The library only ever sets/removes these classes — it never applies
inline styles for anything covered here, so overriding the class is
enough; there's no competing inline style to fight.

| Class | Applied when |
|---|---|
| `.kdl-grid-layout` | Always, on the root element. |
| `.kdl-grid-layout--active-drag` | While any item in this grid has an active drag (raises this grid's own stacking context, relevant for `allowCrossGridDrag`). |
| `.kdl-grid-layout--grid-lines` | `showGridLines` is on. |
| `.kdl-grid-item` | Always, on each item's own root element. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--draggable` | The resolved `isDraggable` is `true` for this item. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--dragging` | This item has an active drag in progress. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--resizing` | This item has an active resize in progress. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--static` | This item's `isStatic` is `true`. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--selected` | This item is part of the current `multiSelect` selection. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--has-header` | The `header` prop was provided. |
| `.kdl-grid-item--rtl` | This item participates in `isMirrored` (RTL). |
| `.kdl-grid-item--show-resize-handles` | The resolved `showResizeHandles` is `true` for this item. |
| `.kdl-grid-item-header` / `.kdl-grid-item-body` | The two regions created when `header` is provided. |
| `.kdl-grid-item-close-button` | The built-in close button, when `showCloseButton` is on. |
| `.kdl-resize-hint--n` / `--s` / `--e` / `--w` / `--ne` / `--nw` / `--se` / `--sw` | The (always-present, invisible-by-default) hit zone for each resize edge/corner actually rendered — see `resizeHandles`. |

```css
/* After importing '@keystone-dashboard-layout/react/style.css' */
.kdl-grid-item.kdl-grid-item--static {
  background-color: #1e293b;
}
```

A real first-fit bin-pack — removing an item from the middle of the grid opens a gap the next added item actually reuses.

import AddRemoveItems from '../../../../components/examples-react/10-add-remove-items.tsx';
import AddRemoveItemsSource from '../../../../components/examples-react/10-add-remove-items.tsx?raw';
import ExampleTryIt from '../../../../components/harness/ExampleTryIt.astro';

<ExampleTryIt code={AddRemoveItemsSource} filename="add-remove-items.tsx" lang="tsx">
  <AddRemoveItems client:visible />
</ExampleTryIt>

Where a newly-added item actually lands is entirely up to the
consumer — the library only places it wherever `x`/`y` say to, then
compacts around it. Appending with `x:0, y:0` (or `y: Infinity`,
placed at the very bottom instead) and letting compaction settle it is
the simplest convention, but it never *reuses a gap* left by a removed
item — a new item always lands in a fresh row even when there's
clearly room higher up.

This demo's own `addItem` does a real first-fit bin-pack instead, via
this package's own exported `findFirstFitSlot` (from
`@keystone-dashboard-layout/core`): remove an item from the middle of
the grid, then add a new one, and it lands in the gap left behind. The
toggle demonstrates a second placement strategy — appending to the end
of the first row specifically, falling back to the general bin-pack
once that row is full.

The two strategies only produce a *visibly different* result once
there's an actual gap for them to disagree about — on a fresh, packed
layout, both fill the first row left-to-right and wrap to a new row
the same way, so toggling it on or off looks identical. To see the
difference: remove item `1` (opening a gap at `x:3`), leave the toggle
on, then add an item — it skips that gap and lands past the row's own
rightmost occupied edge instead, rather than filling it the way the
general bin-pack would.

`onItemClose` fires when the close button is clicked (`showCloseButton`
is on) — pair it with a `.filter()` the same way as above; it
deliberately doesn't remove anything from `layout` itself.

import AlignDistributeSelected from '../../../../components/examples-react/46-align-distribute-selected.tsx';
import AlignDistributeSelectedSource from '../../../../components/examples-react/46-align-distribute-selected.tsx?raw';

<ExampleTryIt code={AlignDistributeSelectedSource} filename="align-distribute-selected.tsx" lang="tsx">

Both are exposed on the [imperative handle](/react/api/interfaces/imperative-handle/),
only meaningful with `multiSelect` on. `alignSelected` treats the
**first-selected item** (insertion order, not an arbitrary one) as the
anchor — it never moves; every other selected item aligns to its edge
or center. Needs at least 2 selected items to do anything.

`distributeSelected` needs at least 3 — the two outermost items (by
actual position, not selection order) stay exactly where they are, and
only what's "in between" spaces out evenly across the span those two
already define, the standard design-tool "distribute" behavior.

Both respect `preventCollision` when it's on — an adjustment that would
land an item on top of a *non-selected* item is skipped for that one
item; landing on another item that's *also* part of the same
align/distribute batch isn't treated as a collision at all, since
that's frequently the whole point of the command.

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `'auto'` (default when unset) | Grows/shrinks to fit content — same as the older `autoSize: true`. In the demo above, this deliberately overflows the dashed frame, since nothing here constrains it. |
| `'fixed'` | No explicit height applied at all — the consumer's own CSS decides. Same as `autoSize: false`. |
| `'scroll'` | Same as `'fixed'`, but also applies an inline `overflow-y: auto`, so content taller than whatever height your own CSS gives it scrolls internally instead of overflowing. |
| `'fit'` | Height locked to `100%` of the parent container, with the same `overflow-y: auto` as `'scroll'` — for a grid meant to fill a fixed-size panel exactly. |

boolean — set `heightMode` explicitly to opt into any of these, no
behavior change for existing consumers who only use `autoSize`.

## Multi-select

Off by default (`multiSelect: false`) — every prior behavior is
completely unaffected when this stays off. When on:

- **Click** an item — selects only it, replacing any prior selection.
- **Shift+click or Ctrl/Cmd+click** — adds/removes that item from the
  current selection additively.
- **Click empty grid background** — clears the selection entirely.

Dragging or resizing any *selected* item while more than one item is
selected moves/resizes every other selected item by the same delta —
also works from the keyboard (arrow keys/Shift+arrow on a focused,
selected item), not just mouse/touch drag.

A passenger that's static, or has `isDraggable`/`isResizable`
explicitly `false` on its own layout entry, never moves or resizes as
part of a group gesture. A passenger's own `minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`
are also respected individually during group resize — see item "d" in
the demo above, which stops at its own `maxW` of 3 even while the
other, unconstrained items keep growing.

:::caution[Deliberately scoped, not fully collision-aware]
The delta is applied directly to every other selected item's position
or size — there's no per-passenger collision detection against
*non-selected* items during the gesture itself. Compaction (per
`compactType`) still runs normally once the gesture ends.
:::

:::note[selectedItems is a snapshot, not reactive state]
Unlike Vue's own template ref (whose `selectedItems` is genuinely
reactive), the imperative handle's `selectedItems` here is a plain
snapshot — reading it directly in JSX won't re-render when selection
changes. Use `onSelectionChanged` (as this example does) to mirror the
current selection into your own React state instead.
:::

import OutsideDropAcceptPayload from '../../../../components/examples-react/34-outside-drop-accept-payload.tsx';
import OutsideDropAcceptPayloadSource from '../../../../components/examples-react/34-outside-drop-accept-payload.tsx?raw';
import ExampleTryIt from '../../../../components/harness/ExampleTryIt.astro';

<ExampleTryIt code={OutsideDropAcceptPayloadSource} filename="outside-drop-accept-payload.tsx" lang="tsx">
  <OutsideDropAcceptPayload client:visible />

`readOutsideDropPayload<T>(dataTransfer, mimeType?)` reads and
JSON-parses a `DataTransfer` payload by MIME type — never throws; a
missing MIME type or malformed JSON both return `null` rather than
propagating a `SyntaxError`. `mimeType` defaults to `'text/plain'`,
matching `dataTransfer.setData`'s own default. Imported from
`@keystone-dashboard-layout/core` directly — this package doesn't
re-export it through its own barrel.

:::note[Why this one starts inside a fixed-height frame]
`layout` starts empty, and `GridLayout`'s own `autoSize` (default
`true`) sizes the container to fit its content — with zero items, that
collapses to almost nothing, leaving no visible area to drop onto at
all. `heightMode="fit"` inside a `.drop-zone-frame` with a real CSS
`height` fixes this: the grid fills that frame regardless of how many
items it currently holds, so there's always a genuine drop target.
:::

:::caution[A real gotcha with native drag-and-drop]
`dataTransfer.getData()` only returns real values during the `drop`
event itself — during `dragenter`/`dragover` (when `outsideDropAccept`
is actually called) it always returns an empty string, regardless of
what the source set. This is a genuine, confirmed bug this example
had at first: `outsideDropAccept` tried to parse the full JSON payload
to check its `kind` field, which silently rejected every drag — real
widget or not — since the payload was never readable at that point.
The browser showed a "not a valid drop target" cursor and the drop
never fired.

The fix: only `dataTransfer.types` (the list of MIME types present,
not their values) is reliably readable during `dragenter`/`dragover`.
This example's drag source now sets a second, value-less MIME type
(`'application/x-widget'`) only on the real widget, and
`outsideDropAccept` checks `dataTransfer.types.includes('application/x-widget')`
instead of trying to read the actual payload. The full JSON payload is
still read via `readOutsideDropPayload` — just at `drop` time, in
`onOutsideDrop`, where `.getData()` genuinely works.
:::

See [Drag, drop from outside](/react/examples/outside-drag-drop/) for
`allowOutsideDrop` itself.

Where a newly-added item actually lands is entirely up to the
consumer — the library only places it wherever `x`/`y` say to, then
compacts around it. Appending with `x:0, y:0` (or `y: Infinity`,
placed at the very bottom instead) and letting compaction settle it is
the simplest convention, but it never *reuses a gap* left by a removed
item — a new item always lands in a fresh row even when there's
clearly room higher up.

This demo's own `addItem` does a real first-fit bin-pack instead, via
this package's own exported `findFirstFitSlot`: remove an item from
the middle of the grid, then add a new one, and it lands in the gap
left behind. The toggle demonstrates a second placement strategy —
appending to the end of the first row specifically, falling back to
the general bin-pack once that row is full.

The two strategies only produce a *visibly different* result once
there's an actual gap for them to disagree about — on a fresh, packed
layout, both fill the first row left-to-right and wrap to a new row
the same way, so toggling it on or off looks identical. To see the
difference: remove item `1` (opening a gap at `x:3`), leave the toggle
on, then add an item — it skips that gap and lands past the row's own
rightmost occupied edge instead, rather than filling it the way the
general bin-pack would.

`.filter()` the same way as above.
What Keystone Dashboard Layout for React is, what you get, and where to go next.

Keystone Dashboard Layout for React is a React component library for building
draggable, resizable, responsive dashboard grids — the kind of UI you'd
use for a customizable analytics dashboard, a widget board, or any screen
where users rearrange content themselves.

It's a TypeScript-first library built on the exact same shared
`@keystone-dashboard-layout/core` algorithms and native, Pointer
Events-based drag/resize engine the Vue package uses — both frameworks
share one implementation of the hard, easy-to-get-subtly-wrong parts
(collision, compaction, responsive breakpoint math) rather than each
maintaining their own copy. React has reached full feature parity with
the Vue package.

## What you get

- **`GridLayout`** — the container. A **fully controlled** component: it
  never mutates the `layout` array (or any item in it) you pass in —
  every drag/resize tick (and the compaction that follows it) is
  reported via `onLayoutChange` with a brand-new array. This is the same
  `layout`/`onLayoutChange` contract `react-grid-layout` itself uses,
  the idiomatic React pattern here rather than Vue's own two-way
  `v-model:layout` binding.
- **`GridItem`** — a single draggable/resizable cell. It only needs an
  `i` matching one of `layout`'s own entries — position, size, and
  `isDraggable`/`isResizable`/`isStatic`/`minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH` all
  live directly on that layout item, not as separate props on this
  component.
- **An imperative handle via `ref`** — `compactNow()`, `rearrange()`,
  `duplicateItem(id)`, `undo()`/`redo()`, `selectItem()`/
  `clearSelection()`, `alignSelected(edge)`/`distributeSelected(axis)`,
  `exportLayoutAsSvg()`, `scrollToItem(id)`/`focusItem(id)`, and more —
  the React equivalent of Vue's own `defineExpose`'d template-ref
  methods, reached via `forwardRef`/`useImperativeHandle` instead.
- **`useLayoutStorage`** and **`useLayoutPresets`** — hooks wrapping
  layout persistence (serializing to/from `localStorage`) and named
  layout presets.

There's no separate exported close-button or drag-handle component here
— a close button is a built-in, per-item opt-in (`showCloseButton` +
an `onItemClose` callback you handle yourself), and any part of an item
is a drag handle by default, restrictable via `dragAllowFrom`/
`dragIgnoreFrom`.

## How it fits together

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { GridLayout, GridItem } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/react';
import '@keystone-dashboard-layout/react/style.css';
import type { TLayout } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/core';

function Dashboard() {
  const [layout, setLayout] = useState<TLayout>([
    { i: 'a', x: 0, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
    { i: 'b', x: 2, y: 0, w: 2, h: 2 },
  ]);

  return (
    <GridLayout layout={layout} onLayoutChange={setLayout}>
      <GridItem i="a">A</GridItem>
      <GridItem i="b">B</GridItem>
    </GridLayout>
  );
}
```

`layout` is a plain array of `{ i, x, y, w, h, ... }` objects — one per
`GridItem`. You own that array; `onLayoutChange` hands you a new one
every time the user drags or resizes something, and you decide what to
do with it (usually just `setLayout`). Everything else (collision
resolution, compaction, responsive breakpoint switching) happens
automatically based on the props you set.

## Where to go next

- [Features](/react/features/) — the full feature list, grouped by area.
- [Components](/react/components/) — full prop/callback reference for `GridLayout` and `GridItem`.
- [API](/react/api/) — exported TypeScript types, interfaces, and enums.

## Design goals

A few decisions that shape how the library behaves, worth knowing up
front:

- **You own the data.** `layout` is a plain, serializable array you
  control — the library never mutates it in place, only ever hands you
  a new one via `onLayoutChange`.
- **Sensible defaults, explicit overrides.** Most behavior (draggable,
  resizable, bounded, etc.) can be set once on `GridLayout` and
  inherited by every item, or overridden per-item when needed.
- **Idiomatic React, not a literal Vue-to-React transliteration.**
  Vue's `provide`/`inject` eventBus becomes React Context, its
  composables become hooks, its named slots become render props
  (`header`, `renderResizeHandle`), and its two-way `v-model` binding
  becomes the standard controlled-component pattern — the same
  underlying behavior, expressed the way each framework actually works.

Both are exposed on the `GridLayout` instance, only meaningful with
`multiSelect` on. `alignSelected` treats the **first-selected item**
(insertion order, not an arbitrary one) as the anchor — it never moves;
every other selected item aligns to its edge or center. Needs at least
2 selected items to do anything.

`distributeSelected` needs at least 3 — the two outermost items (by
actual position, not selection order) stay exactly where they are, and
only what's "in between" spaces out evenly across the span those two
already define, the standard design-tool "distribute" behavior.

Both respect `preventCollision` when it's on — an adjustment that would
land an item on top of a *non-selected* item is skipped for that one
item; landing on another item that's *also* part of the same
align/distribute batch isn't treated as a collision at all, since
that's frequently the whole point of the command.

| Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `'auto'` (default when unset) | Grows/shrinks to fit content — same as the older `autoSize: true`. In the demo above, this deliberately overflows the dashed frame, since nothing here constrains it. |
| `'fixed'` | No explicit height applied at all — the consumer's own CSS decides. Same as `autoSize: false`. |
| `'scroll'` | Same as `'fixed'`, but also applies an inline `overflow-y: auto`, so content taller than whatever height your own CSS gives it scrolls internally instead of overflowing. |
| `'fit'` | Height locked to `100%` of the parent container, with the same `overflow-y: auto` as `'scroll'` — for a grid meant to fill a fixed-size panel exactly. |

`null` (the actual prop default) defers entirely to the older `autoSize`
boolean — set `heightMode` explicitly to opt into any of these, no
behavior change for existing consumers who only use `autoSize`.
is-mirrored flips the entire grid for right-to-left locales — anchor edges, resize direction, and drag math all reverse together.
layout-ready fires once, after every item's size has stabilized; layout-updated fires on mount and after every subsequent change.

values that are still mid-measurement. `layout-updated` fires more
often — once during mount, and again after every subsequent mutation

```ts
gridRef.value.selectItem('a');           // replaces the selection with just 'a'
gridRef.value.selectItem('b', true);     // adds 'b' additively (Shift/Ctrl+click equivalent)
gridRef.value.toggleItemSelection('b');  // toggles 'b' in/out
gridRef.value.deselectItem('a');
gridRef.value.clearSelection();
gridRef.value.selectedItems;             // reactive array of currently-selected ids
```

## Multi-select

Off by default (`multiSelect: false`) — every prior behavior is
completely unaffected when this stays off. When on:

- **Click** an item — selects only it, replacing any prior selection.
- **Shift+click or Ctrl/Cmd+click** — adds/removes that item from the
  current selection additively.
- **Click empty grid background** — clears the selection entirely.

Dragging or resizing any *selected* item while more than one item is
selected moves/resizes every other selected item by the same delta —
also works from the keyboard (arrow keys/Shift+arrow on a focused,
selected item), not just mouse/touch drag.

A passenger that's static, or has `isDraggable`/`isResizable`
explicitly `false`, never moves or resizes as part of a group gesture
— the same guarantee a static item already has against the normal
collision-push cascade. A passenger's own `minW`/`maxW`/`minH`/`maxH`
are also respected individually during group resize, not just clamped
to the anchor's own limits (or a bare floor of 1) — see item "d" in the
demo above, which stops at its own `maxW` of 3 even while the other,
unconstrained items keep growing.

:::caution[Deliberately scoped, not fully collision-aware]
The delta is applied directly to every other selected item's position
or size — there's no per-passenger collision detection against
*non-selected* items during the gesture itself, only the
dragged/resized item gets the usual collision/bounds handling.
Compaction (per `compactType`) still runs normally once the
gesture ends.
:::

Listen for `@selection-changed` (payload: the full current selection as
an array) to react to selection changes, or read the exposed
`selectedItems` directly.

## Custom resize-handle rendering (`#resize-handle` slot)

A named, scoped slot on `GridItem` — receives `{ edge }` (`'n'`, `'s'`,
`'e'`, `'w'`, `'ne'`, `'nw'`, `'se'`, `'sw'`), letting you render
different content per edge/corner if you want. Renders inside the same
small hit-area `showResizeHandles`/`resizeHandleColor` already use for
the color/visibility toggle — both can be combined, or the slot used on
its own for a fully custom icon instead of a plain colored dot.

import OutsideDropAcceptPayload from '../../../../components/examples/34-outside-drop-accept-payload.vue';
import OutsideDropAcceptPayloadSource from '../../../../components/examples/34-outside-drop-accept-payload.vue?raw';
import ExampleTryIt from '../../../../components/harness/ExampleTryIt.astro';

<ExampleTryIt code={OutsideDropAcceptPayloadSource} filename="outside-drop-accept-payload.vue">
  <OutsideDropAcceptPayload client:visible />
</ExampleTryIt>

`readOutsideDropPayload<T>(dataTransfer, mimeType?)` reads and
JSON-parses a `DataTransfer` payload by MIME type — never throws;
a missing MIME type or malformed JSON both return `null` rather than
propagating a `SyntaxError`. `mimeType` defaults to `'text/plain'`,
matching `dataTransfer.setData`'s own default.

:::note[Why this one starts inside a fixed-height frame]
`layout` starts empty, and `GridLayout`'s own `autoSize` (default
`true`) sizes the container to fit its content — with zero items, that
collapses to almost nothing, leaving no visible area to drop onto at
all. `height-mode="fit"` inside a `.drop-zone-frame` with a real CSS
`height` fixes this: the grid fills that frame regardless of how many
items it currently holds, so there's always a genuine drop target.
:::

:::caution[A real gotcha with native drag-and-drop]
`dataTransfer.getData()` only returns real values during the `drop`
event itself — during `dragenter`/`dragover` (when `outsideDropAccept`
is actually called) it always returns an empty string, regardless of
what the source set. This is a genuine, confirmed bug this example
had at first: `outsideDropAccept` tried to parse the full JSON payload
to check its `kind` field, which silently rejected every drag — real
widget or not — since the payload was never readable at that point.
The browser showed a "not a valid drop target" cursor and the drop
never fired.

The fix: only `dataTransfer.types` (the list of MIME types present,
not their values) is reliably readable during `dragenter`/`dragover`.
This example's drag source now sets a second, value-less MIME type
(`'application/x-widget'`) only on the real widget, and
`outsideDropAccept` checks `dataTransfer.types.includes('application/x-widget')`
instead of trying to read the actual payload. The full JSON payload is
still read via `readOutsideDropPayload` — just at `drop` time, in
`@item-dropped-from-outside`, where `.getData()` genuinely works.
:::

See [Drag, drop from outside](/vue/examples/outside-drag-drop/) for
`allowOutsideDrop` itself, and [API → Overview](/vue/api/) for where
`readOutsideDropPayload` is exported from.

to be to another item's edge before it snaps — default `1`. Unlike
[alignment guides](/vue/examples/alignment-guides/) (`showAlignmentGuides`,
purely visual), this actually changes where the item lands: once the
pointer's dragged-to position is within threshold of an edge alignment,
the position adjusts to match it exactly, both in the live placeholder
while dragging and in the final committed position on drop.

Both features can be on at the same time — the visual guide showing
exactly where the magnetic snap is about to lock to.

`undo()`/`redo()`/`canUndo`/`canRedo` are all exposed on the `GridLayout`
instance, the same `ref`-based pattern as `compactNow()`/`scrollToItem()`.
A snapshot is captured at the *start* of a drag/resize and committed at
its *end* — not per intermediate frame — so one undo reverts a whole
gesture at once, not one step per pixel moved. `undoHistoryLimit`
(default `50`) caps how many snapshots `undo()` can step back through.

The default close button rendered inside a `GridItem` when
`showCloseButton` is true. Also exported standalone from the package's
main entry point, in case you want to render the same button somewhere
else (a custom header, say) and wire it to the same removal event
yourself.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { CustomCloseButton } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/vue';

function removeItem(id: string | number): void {
  layout.value = layout.value.filter((item) => item.i !== id);
}
</script>

<template>
  <CustomCloseButton :i="item.i" @remove-grid-item="removeItem" />
</template>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `i` | `string \| number` | `-1` | The id of the `GridItem` this button removes when clicked. `-1` is treated as a "no item" sentinel — clicking with the default value is a no-op, rather than emitting a removal for a nonexistent item. |

## Events

| Event | Payload | When |
|---|---|---|
| `remove-grid-item` | `(i: string \| number)` | The button was clicked with a real `i` set (not the `-1` default). |

## Why you'd use this instead of `showCloseButton`

`showCloseButton` is the right choice for the common case — the built-in
button, styled via the classes documented in
[Styling → GridItem](/vue/components/styling/css-grid-item/). Reach for
`CustomCloseButton` directly when you want the exact same click/removal
behavior but need to place it somewhere `GridItem`'s own internal
rendering doesn't reach — inside a custom header slot, for instance. See
[Custom drag handle & close button](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/)
for a full working example using both `CustomCloseButton` and
`CustomDragElement` together.

A small drag-handle widget, exported for placing inside a `GridItem`'s
slot content when you want dragging restricted to a single handle rather
than the whole item — pair it with `GridItem`'s `dragAllowFrom` prop so
only this element starts a drag.

:::caution[The grab target is a small circle, not the visible button]
The rendered markup is a labeled `<button>` **plus a separate**, small
decorative circle element carrying the `vue-draggable-handle` class —
confirmed directly from the component's own template. `dragAllowFrom`
matches that circle specifically, not the button/text you actually see
labeled. Clicking the visible text does **not** start a drag; only the
small circle (rendered at the widget's own bottom-right corner) does.

Not used anywhere internally in this library — a standalone, opt-in
utility component, exported from the package's main entry point
alongside `CustomCloseButton`.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { CustomDragElement } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <GridItem drag-allow-from=".vue-draggable-handle" :h="item.h" :i="item.i" :w="item.w" :x="item.x" :y="item.y">
    <CustomDragElement text="⠿" />
    Item content
  </GridItem>
</template>
```

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | `'x'` | Label rendered inside the handle's own button. |

## Pairing with `resizeIgnoreFrom`

If the handle sits near a corner, it can land inside the same
edge-proximity margin the resize engine already uses to detect a resize
gesture — meaning grabbing the handle could start a resize instead of
the drag `dragAllowFrom` was meant to restrict things to. Excluding the
handle from `resizeIgnoreFrom` as well is what actually stops the two
from fighting over the same gesture:

```vue
<GridItem
  drag-allow-from=".vue-draggable-handle"
  resize-ignore-from=".vue-draggable-handle"
  ...>
```

See [Custom drag handle & close button](/vue/examples/custom-drag-handle-close-button/)
for a full working example combining this with `CustomCloseButton`.

What Keystone Dashboard Layout for Vue is, what you get, and where to go next.

Keystone Dashboard Layout for Vue is a Vue 3 component library for building
draggable, resizable, responsive dashboard grids — the kind of UI you'd
use for a customizable analytics dashboard, a widget board, or any screen
where users rearrange content themselves.

It's a TypeScript-first library built from the ground up on Vue 3's
Composition API, using a native, Pointer Events-based drag/resize engine
with no third-party runtime dependency for it at all.

## What you get

- **`GridLayout`** — the container. Owns the layout array (position/size
  of every item), responsive breakpoint state, and collision/compaction
  logic.
- **`GridItem`** — a single draggable/resizable cell, rendered inside
  `GridLayout`'s default slot. You control what's inside it — text,
  images, charts, forms, anything.
- **Two small utility components** — `CustomCloseButton` and
  `CustomDragElement` — exported in case you want to reuse the library's
  own default close button or build a dedicated drag handle.

## How it fits together

```vue
<GridLayout v-model:layout="layout">
  <GridItem v-for="item in layout" :key="item.i" v-bind="item">
    <!-- your content -->
  </GridItem>
</GridLayout>
```

`layout` is a plain array of `{ i, x, y, w, h, ... }` objects — one per
`GridItem`. You own that array; the library reads and updates it as the
user drags and resizes things. Everything else (collision resolution,
compaction, responsive breakpoint switching) happens automatically based
on the props you set.

## Where to go next

- [Installation](/vue/guide/installation/) — add the package to your project.
- [Examples](/vue/examples/) — interactive, copy-pasteable examples, from a
  basic grid to responsive breakpoints and drag-drop between grids.
- [Components](/vue/components/) — full prop/event/slot reference for `GridLayout` and `GridItem`.
- [API](/vue/api/) — exported TypeScript types, interfaces, and enums.

## Design goals

A few decisions that shape how the library behaves, worth knowing up
front:

- **You own the data.** The layout array is yours — the library mutates
  it in place / emits updates, but never hides state you can't inspect or
  serialize (see [v-model & save/load layout](/vue/examples/save-load-layout/)).
- **Sensible defaults, explicit overrides.** Most behavior (draggable,
  resizable, bounded, etc.) can be set once on `GridLayout` and inherited
  by every item, or overridden per-item when needed.
- **Composition over configuration objects.** Props map directly to
  documented, individually-typed options rather than one large opaque
  config object — better autocomplete, better documentation per option.

The typed payloads for GridLayout's cross-grid and outside-drop callbacks.
The public methods and fields GridLayoutComponent exposes — the Angular equivalent of Vue's defineExpose or React's imperative handle.

Angular has no separate "imperative handle" type the way React does —
these are simply the `public` methods and fields on the
`GridLayoutComponent` class itself, reached via a template reference
variable:

```ts
import { Component, ViewChild } from '@angular/core';
import { GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/angular';

@Component({
  standalone: true,
  imports: [GridLayoutComponent, GridItemComponent],
  template: `
    <button (click)="grid.compactNow()">Tidy up</button>
    <kdl-grid-layout #grid [layout]="layout" (layoutChange)="layout = $event">
      <!-- ... -->
    </kdl-grid-layout>
  `,
})
export class DashboardComponent {
  @ViewChild('grid') gridRef!: GridLayoutComponent;
  // ...
}
```

A template reference variable (`#grid`, used directly in the template
above via `grid.compactNow()`) works for calling a method from within
the same template. Reach the same instance from your own component
class instead via `@ViewChild('grid')`, as shown.

## Compaction

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `compactNow` | `(): void` | Re-runs compaction on demand — forces real compaction even when `compactType` is `NONE`, unlike the automatic per-tick compaction. |
| `rearrange` | `(): void` | Alias for `compactNow()`. |

## Items

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `duplicateItem` | `(id: string \| number): string \| number \| null` | Clones the item, placing the copy directly below the source. Returns the new item's id, or `null` if `id` doesn't match. |
| `scrollToItem` | `(id: string \| number): void` | Scrolls the item into view, if currently rendered. A no-op (not a throw) on a missing id. |
| `focusItem` | `(id: string \| number): void` | Moves keyboard focus to the item, if currently rendered and focusable. |

## Selection (`multiSelect`)

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `selectedItemIds` | `Set<string \| number>` | The currently-selected item ids. A `Set`, not an array — for O(1) `.has()` lookups. Always empty when `multiSelect` is off. |
| `selectItem` | `(id: string \| number): void` | Selects exactly this item, replacing any existing selection. |
| `deselectItem` | `(id: string \| number): void` | Removes this item from the selection, if present. |
| `toggleItemSelection` | `(id: string \| number): void` | Adds if absent, removes if present. |
| `clearSelection` | `(): void` | Empties the selection entirely. |
| `alignSelected` | `(edge: TAlignEdge): void` | Aligns every selected item to the given edge/center of the anchor (the first-selected item, which never moves). A no-op with fewer than 2 items selected. |
| `distributeSelected` | `(axis: TDistributeAxis): void` | Evenly spaces selected items along the given axis; the two outermost stay fixed. A no-op with fewer than 3 items selected. |

## Undo/redo (`enableUndoRedo`)

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `undo` | `(): void` | Reverts to the most recently captured pre-gesture snapshot. A no-op when `canUndo` is `false`. |
| `redo` | `(): void` | Reapplies the most recently undone state. A no-op when `canRedo` is `false`. |
| `canUndo` | `boolean` | Whether `undo()` currently has a snapshot to revert to. |
| `canRedo` | `boolean` | Whether `redo()` currently has a snapshot to reapply. |

:::note[canUndo/canRedo are plain fields, not signals or observables]
Reading `gridRef.canUndo` from your own component class won't
automatically re-render your own template when it changes — Angular's
change detection picks it up on the *grid's own* next check (already
triggered internally via `markForCheck()` whenever these change), but
if you're mirroring the value into your own component's state for a
disabled-button binding, you'll need your own mechanism to know when
to re-read it, the same class of consideration React's snapshot-style
`canUndo`/`canRedo` on its own imperative handle requires.
:::

The ref-based API GridLayout exposes — the React equivalent of Vue's defineExpose template-ref methods.

Attach a `ref` to `GridLayout` to reach these — the React equivalent of
Vue's own `defineExpose`'d template-ref methods, via `forwardRef`/
`useImperativeHandle` instead.

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { GridLayout, type IGridLayoutHandle } from '@keystone-dashboard-layout/react';

function Dashboard() {
  const gridRef = useRef<IGridLayoutHandle>(null);

  return (
    <>
      <button onClick={() => gridRef.current?.compactNow()}>Tidy up</button>
      <GridLayout ref={gridRef} layout={layout} onLayoutChange={setLayout}>
        {/* ... */}
      </GridLayout>
    </>
  );
}
```

Only `layout` is required — everything else has a default.
`GridLayoutComponent` is a **fully controlled** component: it never
mutates `layout` in place. Callbacks are `@Output()` `EventEmitter`s
here — this table includes them alongside the `@Input()`s. Several
boolean/number `@Input()`s here cascade a grid-wide default down to
every descendant `GridItemComponent` via a DI-scoped event bus; a
matching `@Input()` on that item overrides it (`null` defers to the
cascade). See each row's own note.

## Core

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `layout` | `TLayout` (required) | — | The layout array — used for the container's own `autoSize` height calculation and as the basis for collision resolution. Rendering each item is your own responsibility, via `GridItemComponent`. |
| `layoutChange` | `EventEmitter<TLayout>` | — | Emits a brand-new layout array whenever a drag end, resize end, or the compaction that follows either changes it. The input `layout` `@Input()` itself is never mutated. |

## Sizing & columns

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `colNum` | `number` | `12` | Maximum number of columns. Ignored while `responsive` is on. |
| `rowHeight` | `number` | `150` | Height of one grid row, in pixels. |
| `margin` | `[number, number]` | `[10, 10]` | `[horizontal, vertical]` spacing between items, in pixels. |
| `maxRows` | `number` | `Infinity` | Maximum number of rows the layout may grow to — cascaded, unconditionally overriding a standalone `GridItemComponent`'s own `maxRows` `@Input()` (this one field has no per-item override in Angular either, matching Vue). |
| `autoSize` | `boolean` | `true` | Grows/shrinks the container's height to fit the layout's content. Ignored once `heightMode` is set to anything other than `null`. |
| `heightMode` | `'auto' \| 'fixed' \| 'scroll' \| 'fit' \| null` | `null` | How the container's height is determined. `null` defers to `autoSize`. `'auto'`: today's `autoSize: true` behavior. `'fixed'`: no explicit height. `'scroll'`: same as `'fixed'`, plus `overflow-y: auto`. `'fit'`: height locked to `100%` of the parent, with the same `overflow-y: auto` as `'scroll'`. |
| `useCssTransforms` | `boolean` | `true` | Positions items via CSS `transform: translate3d(...)` instead of `top`/`left`. |
| `transformScale` | `number` | `1` | Compensates drag/resize pixel math for a scaled ancestor (e.g. a zoomed-out canvas view) — cascaded to every descendant `GridItemComponent`. |

## Drag & resize defaults

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isDraggable` | `boolean` | `true` | Cascaded default for items that don't set their own `isDraggable`. |
| `isResizable` | `boolean` | `true` | Cascaded default for items that don't set their own `isResizable`. |
| `isBounded` | `boolean` | `false` | Cascaded default for items that don't set their own `isBounded`. |
| `enableEditMode` | `boolean` | `true` | Cascaded, grid-wide master interactivity switch — `false` disables `tabindex`/`role`/the keyboard-instructions span/the close button across the whole grid at once. Does **not** gate the native drag/resize engine itself, nor the keyboard handler's own guard — both read the raw resolved `isDraggable`/`isResizable` directly, matching Vue's own identical asymmetry. |
| `showResizeHandles` | `boolean` | `false` | Grid-wide default for whether the 8 resize-hint spans are visibly styled, applied via `--kdl-resize-handle-color` — inherited naturally through the DOM, not via the eventBus. A per-item override exists. |
| `resizeHandleColor` | `string` | `'rgb(94 94 94 / 45%)'` | CSS color for the visible resize-handle affordance, when `showResizeHandles` is on. |

## Collision & compaction

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preventCollision` | `boolean` | `false` | Blocks a drag/resize that would collide, instead of pushing the other item. |
| `compactType` | `ECompactType` | `ECompactType.VERTICAL` | Selects one of five built-in compaction strategies. Ignored when `compactor` is set. |
| `compactor` | `ICompactor \| null` | `null` | Overrides the built-in compaction algorithm entirely. Purely additive — `compactType` keeps working normally when this isn't set. |
| `horizontalShift` | `boolean` | `false` | Pushes colliding items left/right instead of down, during an active drag — a pure pass-through to `core`'s own `moveElement`. |
| `restoreOnDrag` | `boolean` | `false` | While dragging, keeps other items from compacting past their pre-drag position until the drag ends. |
| `distributeEvenly` | `boolean` | `false` | On a responsive breakpoint change that shrinks `colNum`, spreads an out-of-bounds item to the next available slot instead of clamping it to the right edge. |
| `snapToGrid` | `boolean` | `false` | Magnetically snaps a dragged item's edge to another item's edge — changes where the item lands, unlike `showAlignmentGuides`. |
| `snapThreshold` | `number` | `1` | How close (in grid units) an edge needs to be to snap, when `snapToGrid` is on. |
| `showAlignmentGuides` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows guide lines while dragging/resizing wherever edges line up — visual only. |
| `showSpacingGuides` | `boolean` | `false` | Shows a labeled distance badge between the active item and its nearest neighbor. |
| `moveBlockedByCollision` | `EventEmitter<string \| number>` | — | Emits this item's own id when `preventCollision` actually constrained a drag (blocked entirely) or a resize (clamped, can still partially grow). |

## Multi-select & undo/redo

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `multiSelect` | `boolean` | `false` | Enables click/Ctrl-click/Shift-click (range) multi-item selection, and group move/resize for the selection. |
| `selectionChanged` | `EventEmitter<(string \| number)[]>` | — | Emits the full, current selection whenever it changes. |
| `enableUndoRedo` | `boolean` | `false` | Enables `undo()`/`redo()` (public methods) and the `canUndo`/`canRedo` public fields. Snapshots are taken at drag start, resize start, and before `compactNow()`/`alignSelected()`/`distributeSelected()`. |

## Responsive

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `responsive` | `boolean` | `false` | Enables breakpoint switching — `colNum` becomes derived instead of the plain `@Input()`. |
| `breakpoints` | `IBreakpoints` | `{ xxl: 1600, xl: 1400, lg: 1200, md: 996, sm: 768, xs: 480, xxs: 0 }` | Container-width thresholds per breakpoint. All 7 standard keys required. |
| `cols` | `IColumns` | `{ xxl: 12, xl: 12, lg: 12, md: 10, sm: 6, xs: 4, xxs: 2 }` | Column count per breakpoint. |

## Cross-grid & outside drag-and-drop

| Input/Output | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowCrossGridDrag` | `boolean` | `false` | Enables dragging an item between two `GridLayoutComponent` instances that both have this set, via a real first-fit bin-pack. |
| `disableExternalDrop` | `boolean` | `false` | This grid rejects incoming cross-grid drops. Its own items can still be dragged out. Only relevant when `allowCrossGridDrag` is on. |
| `layoutId` | `string \| null` | auto-generated | This grid's own identifier for the cross-grid registry and event payloads. |
| `crossGridItemDropped` | `EventEmitter<ICrossGridItemDropped>` | — | Emits on the target grid when another grid's item is dropped and accepted. |
| `crossGridDropRejected` | `EventEmitter<ICrossGridDropRejected>` | — | Emits on the target grid when it rejects an incoming drop. |
| `allowOutsideDrop` | `boolean` | `false` | Accepts a native HTML5 drag-and-drop from outside the grid system entirely (e.g. a plain `draggable="true"` element). |
| `outsideDropWidth` | `number` | `2` | Width, in grid units, of the live drop-position placeholder. |
| `outsideDropHeight` | `number` | `2` | Height, in grid units, of the live drop-position placeholder. |
| `outsideDropAccept` | `((dataTransfer: DataTransfer \| null) => boolean) \| null` | `null` (accepts everything) | Called on every `dragenter`/`dragover`/`drop` to decide whether the current drag is a valid outside-drop at all — must check `dataTransfer.types`, not `.getData()`, since the latter only returns real values at `drop` time. |
| `itemDroppedFromOutside` | `EventEmitter<{ dataTransfer, h, w, x, y }>` | — | Emits when an accepted native drag is dropped. Does not itself add anything to `layout` — read `dataTransfer` yourself (`readOutsideDropPayload` from `core` is built for this) and apply the result. |

Every prop GridLayout accepts, including callbacks, with defaults.

Only `layout` is required — everything else has a default.
`GridLayout` is a **fully controlled** component: it never mutates
`layout` in place. Callbacks are ordinary props here (there's no
separate "events" mechanism the way Vue emits — this table includes
them alongside the setter-style props). Most boolean/number props here
have a matching field on [`ILayoutItem`](/react/api/) that can override
it per-item; see each prop's note.

| `className` | `string` | — | Applied to the root element, alongside the library's own `kdl-grid-layout` class. |
